## GET /v1/prism/leads - 50 credits (custom)

Runs three exact-intent phrases ('alternative to X', 'X vs', 'switching from X') through content_analysis search in parallel, plus a Reddit (sort=new) and a Hacker News leg, then dedupes them into one feed. Since methodology leads/2 the ranking is judged: an AI classifier reads each candidate and answers five narrow questions (what the author is doing, whether the row is about the competitor product rather than a namesake, whether the author is a vendor, whether your offer would help them, how urgent the need is), and code combines those answers with recency and engagement into lead_score = (0.35 x P(asking, comparing or switching) + 0.20 x P(fits offer) + 0.15 x urgency/3 + 0.15 x recency + 0.15 x engagement) x P(about) x (1 - P(vendor)). Each lead carries intent { label, probabilities, about, seller, fits_offer, urgency, confidence } and lead_score; the label reads 'uncertain' when the classifier has no clear winner. Rows with P(about) below 0.3 (the snowflake on a Christmas jumper) are removed and their URLs listed in dropped_ids. The keyword intent_score and phrase_matched from leads-v1 are still on every row, and if the classifier is unavailable the feed falls back to that keyword order with _warnings: ['intent_unavailable'], intent: null and lead_score: null ('intent_partial' when only some rows could be judged). Conversation-level intent only: page-level matching, no author PII harvesting (web leads carry no handle by design, and no handle is sent to the classifier). Coverage core is the three CA legs and does not depend on the classifier: <0.5 succeed → 50% refund; all five legs fail → full refund. Registers cleanly for a recurring-lead-feed monitor.

**Use when** you want to find buying-intent conversations without writing and scoring your own searches across the web, Reddit, and Hacker News.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `competitor` (required) - The competitor/product to mine alternative-seeking conversations for (≤80 chars). · e.g. `notion`
- `product_category` (optional, string) - Optional disambiguator appended to the social queries to cut cross-domain noise (e.g. 'project management'). · e.g. `project management`
- `freshness` (optional, string) - Recency floor. Nd/Nw/Nm (e.g. 30d) or an ISO date. Default 30d. · e.g. `30d`
- `include` (optional, string) - Set `comments` to attach top-thread Reddit comments to the top leads.
- `limit` (optional, integer) - Max leads in the fused feed (1-100, default 50).
- `offer` (optional, string) - What you sell, in one or two plain sentences (max 300 chars). Used to judge whether each author would plausibly be helped by it (intent.fits_offer). Default: 'alternatives to {competitor}'.

**Response** `Analytics`. Fields not published yet - call once with a small limit; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=prism/leads` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/leads" \
  --data-urlencode "competitor=notion" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/lookup - free (0 credits)

Sniffs the platform + endpoint from a URL and returns that endpoint's unified data, with no surcharge. You pay the resolved endpoint's own cost. The join key the whole API runs on is `url`. Takes an ITEM link (a post, video, pin, tweet, repo, product or track), not a profile or channel link, on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X/Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest, Reddit, Threads, Rumble, Truth Social, GitHub, Amazon and Spotify. The `resolved` block names the platform, endpoint, and archetype of the response so agents know the shape that follows; `legs[]` reports the dispatched call's status, cost, and latency.

**Use when** you have a URL but do not know which platform endpoint fits, so you can skip writing your own link parsing and routing.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Pricing** the resolved endpoint's own price, with no routing surcharge: 1 credit for most social lookups and 5 for the advanced ones (Amazon, LinkedIn). The `resolved.endpoint` field in the response names the endpoint that was charged.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Absolute http(s) URL of a single post, video, product or repo. Profile, channel and storefront URLs are NOT accepted: use that platform's own `/profile` endpoint for those. · e.g. `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ`
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV of optional flags to forward verbatim to the resolved endpoint (e.g. `trim`). Each member must be an optional param of that endpoint.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data`, `{ computed, legs, post, resolved }` (inferred from a sample): `computed.content_category`, `computed.engagement_rate`, `computed.estimated_reach`, `computed.language`, `legs`, `post.author.avatar_url`, `post.author.display_name`, `post.author.username` (+35 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/lookup" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/mentions - 1-9 credits (request-shaped)

Pass handle (the @ is optional), or url (a link or a link prefix), or name on its own. platforms defaults to twitter, reddit, facebook. Opt in to instagram for posts that tag the handle, or web (url only) for a web page that contains the link. since is YYYY-MM-DD. include_self defaults to false and drops the account's own rows. Each kept row has match_kind reply, retweet, mention or tag. Unverified rows are dropped and counted in dropped_unverified. Url mode adds first_seen for the link. name is judged; a handle or a url is checked in code and is not judged. If that judgment is unavailable the rows are kept and warnings says why. Instagram comments on unknown posts cannot be searched, and Instagram caption mentions cannot. TikTok comments on unknown posts cannot be searched. Threads search is weak: measured 23/09/2026 it returned no row containing the handle, so Threads is not searched. Facebook post search returned no row containing the handle or the link on the same day, so Facebook is not searched. TikTok search for @handle returned no row containing that @, so TikTok is not searched. Bluesky has no search endpoint. LinkedIn is not covered. Private or deleted content is not covered. This is a first page of each search, not an index.

**Use when** you want to find public mentions of an account or a link when you do not already know the post. It is a first page, not an index. **Not for** brand-wide volume, trend or sentiment, since it reads only the first page of each search (prism/brand-mentions, content_analysis/search).
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · cache 1800 s
**Pricing** 1 credit for each X or Reddit page, 5 for an Instagram tag page, 1 for a web page. A default call holds 3. A page with no verified row is refunded. Facebook, Threads and TikTok are not searched.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `handle` (optional, string) - Account handle, with or without @. Checked in code. Not combined with name. · e.g. `nasa`
- `url` (optional, string) - A link or a link prefix, such as example.com/news. Checked in code. Not combined with name.
- `name` (optional, string) - A display name, 2 to 120 characters, passed on its own. Each row is judged. A failed judgment keeps the rows.
- `platforms` (optional, string) - Comma-separated subset of twitter, reddit, facebook, threads, instagram, tiktok, web. Default twitter, reddit, facebook. Instagram needs a handle. Web needs a url. Facebook, Threads and TikTok are accepted and not searched.
- `since` (optional, string) - Only keep rows published on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. On X it is also part of the search.
- `include_self` (optional, boolean) - When true, keep rows whose author is the handle. Default false.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `handle`, `url`, `name`.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `dropped_unverified.reddit`, `dropped_unverified.twitter`, `first_seen`, `handle`, `include_self`, `legs`, `mentions`, `mode` (+5 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/mentions" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=nasa" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

Lists a GitHub org's repositories, picks the top N by stars (forks/archived filtered), and runs the repo/dossier composite on each in parallel, folded into an org-level rollup. Metered: 1cr to resolve the org + 5cr per repo dossiered; the unused per-repo credits are refunded down to the dossiers that actually succeeded. The org repo-list leg is critical (unknown org → 404 + full refund).

**Use when** you want to size up a whole organization in one call instead of listing the repositories and then pulling a report for each one.

- `repos` (optional, integer) - How many top repos to dossier (1-10, default 5): drives the metered price. · e.g. `5`


## POST /v1/prism/post-stats - 1-500 credits (request-shaped)

Bulk stats refresh for verification loops (clipper payouts). POST a JSON body with a `urls` array (1-100 mixed-platform post links); returns one row per URL: platform, status (ok / not_found / error / unsupported), the unified engagement block (views/likes/comments/shares/saves/reposts), and a server `fetched_at` timestamp: in input order. An Instagram row carries the same counts as `GET /v1/instagram/post/stats`, including the save count and the repost count when Instagram's response includes them (for a save count on every reel, use that endpoint with include=saves), and accepts every Instagram permalink form, including `instagram.com/<handle>/p/<code>/` as returned by `/v1/instagram/profile/posts`. Per-URL isolation: one dead link never fails the batch. Metered per successful URL at that URL's platform rate: 1 credit on most platforms, 2 credits for an Instagram post (5 on the single Instagram post stats endpoint) and 5 for LinkedIn post stats; dead, errored, and unsupported URLs are refunded, so you pay exactly for the counts you got. Never cached (every call reads the live count). Optionally streams Server-Sent Events when the client sends `Accept: text/event-stream`.

**Use when** you want to refresh engagement across many posts at once, with each link isolated so one dead URL never fails the rest of the batch. **Not for** one post's full detail, caption and author (tiktok/post, youtube/video).
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · not cached
**Pricing** 1 credit per successful URL on most platforms, 2 on Instagram and 5 on LinkedIn, charged at each URL's own platform rate. Up to 100 URLs per call: the call holds the summed worst case up front (a 100-URL Instagram batch holds 200) and refunds every dead, errored and unsupported URL, so you pay for exactly the rows that returned counts.
**Streaming** Optional SSE - send `Accept: text/event-stream` for incremental frames, or omit it for one JSON body.
**Paging** none

**Body params** (JSON)

- `urls` (required) - JSON array of 1-100 absolute http(s) post URLs (mixed platforms allowed). · e.g. `["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"]`
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV subset of views,likes,comments,shares,saves,reposts to trim each row's engagement block.

**Response** `Analytics`. Fields not published yet - call it once; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=prism/post-stats` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/post-stats" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls":["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"]}'
```

Resolves a product on Amazon (ASIN) + Google Shopping (gid) + Trustpilot (when resolving by `query`, a judgment picks the result that is the product itself, not an accessory or reseller, and reports it in `entity_resolution`) and pulls each source's reviews, folded into a per-source rating summary (listed aggregate preferred over sample mean), a retailer matrix, and an LLM topic pass with per-topic rating impact (the model only assigns review ids: averages are recomputed in code). ## POST /v1/prism/profiles - 1-250 credits (request-shaped)

Batch profile lookup for handle vetting. POST a JSON body with an `items` array of 1-50 `{ platform, handle, custom_id? }` objects (handle accepts an @handle, a bare handle, or a pasted profile URL); returns one row per item: the canonical Author object (same shape as the single GET profile endpoint), a `status` of ok / not_found / unsupported / error / deferred, the caller's `custom_id` echoed, and the credits that row cost: in input order. Per-item isolation: one dead or private handle never fails the batch. Billing is per item at each platform's own credit tier (most platforms 1 credit; LinkedIn 5); only successful rows are charged, everything else is refunded. Supported platforms: instagram, tiktok, youtube, twitter, threads, twitch, snapchat, truthsocial, bluesky, kwai, linkedin, facebook. Never cached. Optionally streams Server-Sent Events when the client sends `Accept: text/event-stream`. Send `include: "posts"` (up to 25 items) to add each handle's first page of posts beside its profile: every ok row gains a `posts` block with the same post rows, `next_cursor` and `has_more` as that handle's own post list endpoint (`endpoint` names it: instagram profile/posts, tiktok profile/videos, youtube channel/videos, twitter user/tweets, threads user/posts, facebook profile/posts; other platforms answer `posts.status: "unsupported"`). `since` on the body and `stop_at_id` on an item stop each page at a date or at a post you already hold, as on those endpoints, and `posts.stopped_at` says which. The profile in `data` is unchanged.

**Use when** you want to vet many handles at once instead of calling the profile endpoint per handle; creator-card is for one handle across several platforms. **Not for** one handle across several platforms (prism/creator-card), or a single profile where its own endpoint is simpler (tiktok/profile, instagram/profile).
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · not cached
**Pricing** 1 credit per successful row on most platforms and 5 on LinkedIn, charged at each handle's own platform tier. Up to 50 items per call: the call holds the summed worst case up front and refunds every not_found, unsupported, errored and deferred row. With include: "posts" (up to 25 items) a row also costs its post list page, 1 credit, charged only when that page came back with posts.
**Streaming** Optional SSE - send `Accept: text/event-stream` for incremental frames, or omit it for one JSON body.
**Paging** none

**Body params** (JSON)

- `items` (required) - JSON array of 1-50 items (1-25 with include: "posts"). Each item is `{ "platform": "tiktok", "handle": "@scout2015", "custom_id"?: "…", "stop_at_id"?: "…" }`. `handle` accepts an @handle, a bare handle, or a pasted profile URL. `stop_at_id` (only with include: "posts") is the id or URL of the newest post you already hold for that handle: its page stops just before it. · e.g. `[{"platform":"tiktok","handle":"@scout2015"},{"platform":"linkedin","handle":"williamhgates","custom_id":"vet-1"}]`
- `include` (optional, enum: posts) - Optional. "posts" adds the handle's first page of posts to every ok row (`posts`), for the price of that page (1 credit), charged only when the page came back with posts. Caps the batch at 25 items.
- `since` (optional, string) - Optional, with include: "posts". Only posts published on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO 8601 timestamp); each page stops at the first older post and `posts.stopped_at` is `since`.

**Response** `Analytics`. Fields not published yet - call it once; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=prism/profiles` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/profiles" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":[{"platform":"tiktok","handle":"@scout2015"},{"platform":"linkedin","handle":"williamhgates","custom_id":"vet-1"}]}'
```

## GET /v1/prism/reputation - 30 credits (custom)

Resolves (a judgment picks which search result is the brand or app itself, reported in `entity_resolution`) and pulls reviews from Trustpilot, the Google Play + App Store listings, Google Business (and TripAdvisor when `place` is set), plus a content_analysis web-sentiment + rating-distribution read, then blends them into a renormalized weighted composite_score (company vs product axes) with per-source ratings (listed aggregate preferred over sample mean) and an LLM-themed pros/cons pass (counts + verbatim quotes recomputed in code). **Use when** you want it for an overall read on how a company is seen; product-reviews is the version for one specific product rather than the company.

**Query params**

- `brand` (required) - The brand/business/domain to assess. · e.g. `Notion`
- `sources` (optional, string) - CSV subset of trustpilot,google_play,app_store,google,tripadvisor,web (default the core set). · e.g. `trustpilot,google_play,app_store,web`
- `country` (optional, string) - Marketplace or locale, as a location name or numeric code (look one up with `GET /v1/content_analysis/locations`). Defaults to United States.
- `depth` (optional, integer) - Reviews per source (Trustpilot clamped ≤20).
- `place` (optional, string) - Set to enable the place-based legs (Google Business + TripAdvisor).
- `axis` (optional, enum: company | product | both) - Which reputation axis to headline: company, product, or both (default).
- `app_store_id` (optional, string) - App Store id to anchor that axis directly (skips resolver).
- `google_play_id` (optional, string) - Google Play id to anchor that axis directly (skips resolver).
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV subset of `themes`, `response_rate`, `languages` (default: all three). Naming a subset TRIMS the report to those blocks; an unknown member or an empty value is a 400.

**Response** `Analytics`. Fields not published yet - call it once; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=prism/reputation` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/reputation" \
  --data-urlencode "brand=Notion" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/review-integrity - 30 credits (custom)

Computes a documented, reproducible integrity grade for a product or brand by comparing ratings across Amazon, Google Shopping, Trustpilot, and the open web: cross-source rating divergence (Welch t-test), web-distribution bimodality (Sarle's coefficient), unsolicited-forum tone contrast, and spam-domain clustering. The grade uses no AI: every number is a published formula (`methodology_version`). When you pass `query`, a judgment picks which search result is the product itself and not an accessory or reseller (`entity_resolution`, with `resolved_by` and a confidence per source); it falls back to the first result, and a source with no matching listing is dropped with an `entity_not_found:<source>` warning. Returns the grade, per-signal evidence, per-source ratings, the divergence pair, and the raw sampled reviews. Reviewer-history tests are flagged `unavailable` (no upstream reviewer-profile source). Anchor on `asin`/`gid` for precision or `query` to auto-resolve. Commerce data takes 20-60s.

**Use when** you suspect inflated or paid reviews; product-reviews tells you what buyers said, this tells you whether to believe the ratings.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `query` (optional, string) - Product or brand name to evaluate. · e.g. `AirPods Pro 3`
- `asin` (optional, string) - Amazon ASIN to anchor the Amazon axis directly (skips product-search).
- `gid` (optional, string) - Google product id (gid) to anchor the Google Shopping axis (NOT the catalogid product.id).
- `sources` (optional, string) - CSV subset of amazon,google_shopping,trustpilot,web,forums (default all). · e.g. `amazon,trustpilot,forums`
- `country` (optional, string) - Marketplace country, as a location name or numeric code (look one up with `GET /v1/content_analysis/locations`). Defaults to United States.

**Constraints**

- Provide at least one of `query`, `asin`, `gid`.

**Response** `Analytics`. Fields not published yet - call it once; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=prism/review-integrity` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/review-integrity" \
  --data-urlencode "query=AirPods Pro 3" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/share-of-voice - 20-200 credits (request-shaped)

Per brand, fans out to content_analysis summary/phrase-trends/sentiment plus /search/everywhere (consuming the real per-platform items_by_source counts, not the capped fused list), then computes a published-formula SOV (web + social, equal-weighted by default), optional true-share-of-category (numeric `category_code`), and ESOV (`market_shares`, Binet/Field: a planning signal, not a growth guarantee). The web share is divided from the windowed phrase-trends sum over `date_from`..`date_to`, never from the upstream's all-time `total_count`, which is censored at 4,000,000 and would tie any two brands above that cap at exactly 50/50; the all-time figure still rides along per brand as `web_mentions_all_time` with a `web_mentions_all_time_censored` flag. One axis is chosen for the whole table and named in `methodology.web_axis`, so a brand whose timeline is unavailable can never be compared against a rival's on a different footing; if no brand's timeline is available the table falls back to the all-time totals and `_warnings` states that your window was not applied, and if those totals are censored it returns no web share at all instead of a fabricated tie. Every measured brand is scored on the SAME evidence basis: if one brand's social leg returns nothing, the whole table drops to the axes every brand has, `methodology.basis` names it, and `_warnings` says which brand caused it, so the column is always a real share rather than a mix of formulas. `methodology` ships the weights, the formula, the axis and the denominators, so you can recompute any share by hand from the same payload. With the social leg on, each brand's highest-engagement social rows (up to `methodology.about_brand.max_rows_per_brand`) are also judged for whether they are about that brand at all, and a second set of numbers is published next to the first, never in place of it: `engagement_sum_about_brand`, `social_sov_pct_about_brand` and `sov_pct_about_brand` leave out the rows under `methodology.about_brand.about_brand_at_or_above`, and `per_brand[].about_brand` lists the excluded row ids, their engagement, and the negative mentions by aspect. The web axis is an index count and is not cleaned. If any brand's rows could not be judged the cleaned numbers are null for the whole table and `_warnings` says `about_brand_unavailable`. The price is the same either way. Metered at 40cr/brand (20 web-only); a brand whose social search half-failed is automatically cheaper, with the reason legible in `legs[]` + per-brand `coverage`.

**Use when** you want to compare brands against each other in one call, where brand-mentions covers a single keyword with no competitive split. **Not for** one keyword's trend and sentiment (prism/brand-mentions), and it needs two to five brands, so not for a single brand.
**Cost** price depends on how many items the request sends or returns · cache 1800 s
**Pricing** 40 credits per brand with the social leg, which is the default, or 20 per brand for the web-only read. Up to 5 brands per call, so the 200-credit ceiling is 5 brands with social and dropping `social` from `include` halves it. Price the call as `brands x per-brand` before you send it - this is the most expensive composite on the API.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `brands` (required) - 2-5 competitor brand names (CSV). · e.g. `notion,coda,airtable`
- `category_code` (optional, string) - Numeric category-taxonomy code for true-share-of-category (look one up with `GET /v1/content_analysis/categories`).
- `market_shares` (optional, string) - JSON map of real market share per brand (fraction or %), e.g. {"notion":0.4,"coda":0.25,"airtable":0.35}, to compute ESOV.
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV toggles (default `emotions,social`). Drop `social` for the cheaper web-only variant; drop `emotions` to skip the sentiment leg. The emotion overlay is third-party NLP passed through unmodified and is not scoped to your date window; `methodology.sentiment_provenance` states that on every response that carries it. · e.g. `social,emotions`
- `page_type` (optional, enum: ecommerce | news | blogs | message-boards | organization) - Optional surface filter forwarded to the content_analysis legs.
- `date_from` (optional, string) - Window start (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to 90 days ago.
- `date_to` (optional, string) - Window end (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today.
- `brand_descriptions` (optional, string) - Optional JSON map of a one-line description per brand, e.g. {"notion":"the workspace app"}, used to tell a brand apart from its namesakes.

**Response** `Analytics`. Fields not published yet - call it once; `/v1/utility/endpoint?id=prism/share-of-voice` serves the current contract.

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/share-of-voice" \
  --data-urlencode "brands=notion,coda,airtable" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/trend-board - 30 credits (custom)

Pass country_code (an ISO code Google Trends covers, such as DE). The board is computed live for this call and nothing is stored between calls, so there is no history and no days parameter: repeat calls within 15 minutes are served from cache. `breakout_posts` are videos on TikTok's local feed for that country, registered there, whose views are at least 3 times the median of the author's own recent posts (pinned posts and posts under 48 hours are left out, at least 8 posts are compared, and rows without enough posts are counted, not shown). `rising_sounds` are the sounds used most on that feed, with how many of each sound's first page of videos are from the last 3 days and whether it is a returning or new sound. `rising_hashtags` are TikTok's own hashtag board for the country, with growth from its daily popularity curve and the first day in the window it was non-zero. `rising_searches` are Google Trends Trending Now, where Google's own start time is the first-seen date. `sources` and `unavailable` say which parts answered. TikTok's hashtag board covers 27 markets; elsewhere that section is empty and says why. No language model is used. Music charts and Pinterest Trends are not included yet. The price is provisional.

**Use when** you want to scan a country for trends before you have a term to search. The board is computed on each call and keeps no history.
**Cost** cache 900 s
**Pricing** 30 credits flat (provisional). One call reads TikTok's local feed, TikTok's hashtag board, Google Trending Now, up to 5 author pages and up to 3 sounds. A source that does not answer is listed under unavailable and its section is empty. Only a call where the feed, the hashtag board and Google Trending Now all fail is refunded.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `country_code` (required) - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as DE, US or KR. Any country Google Trends Trending Now covers. · e.g. `DE`
- `period` (optional, enum: 7 | 30) - 7 (default) or 30. The window of TikTok's hashtag board. Google Trending Now is always read over its longest window, 7 days.
- `limit` (optional, integer, 1-10) - Rows per section, 1 to 10. Default 10.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `breakout_posts`, `country`, `generated_at`, `period_days`, `policy_version`, `rising_hashtags`, `rising_searches`, `rising_sounds` (+2 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/trend-board" \
  --data-urlencode "country_code=DE" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/truthsocial-pulse - 20 credits (custom)

Fetches a Truth Social profile + recent posts, drills the top posts for full detail (the F13 post-detail path), and runs a content_analysis news echo for the handle, folded into a deterministic activity/sentiment pulse with stable keys + a methodology_version. The profile leg is critical (404 → full refund); posts/drill/news degrade. No Truth Social search exists upstream. This is handle-scoped.

**Use when** you want to monitor one Truth Social account in a single request, since the platform has no search and you would otherwise chain profile, post, and news calls.
**Cost** cache 1800 s
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - The Truth Social handle (no @). · e.g. `realDonaldTrump`
- `drill` (optional, integer) - How many top posts to drill for full detail (0 to skip). · e.g. `5`
- `posts` (optional, integer) - How many recent posts to pull (window cap).
- `news_query` (optional, string) - Override the content_analysis news keyword (defaults to the handle/display name).
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV subset of posts,news to trim which legs run.
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque pagination cursor for the posts leg.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `account.author.avatar_url`, `account.author.bio`, `account.author.display_name`, `account.author.followers`, `account.author.following`, `account.author.id`, `account.author.joined_at`, `account.author.likes_count` (+30 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/truthsocial-pulse" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=realDonaldTrump" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/video-intel - 5-15 credits (request-shaped)

Fans out the video detail, comments, an optional transcript (10cr, never charged when the video has none), and ≤3 commenter profiles, folding them into one unified payload. Every leg joins on the same video `url`. Sync by default; streams Server-Sent Events when `include=transcript` (the transcript leg can take 20s+). `legs[]` reports each fired leg's status, cost, and latency; `coverage` + `partial_failure` flag any degraded leg. Commenter profiles ship for TikTok + Instagram in v1.

**Use when** you want to build a full picture of a YouTube, TikTok, Rumble, or Instagram video in one call instead of chaining detail, comments, and transcript calls. **Not for** only a video's details (youtube/video, tiktok/post) or only its whole comment thread (prism/comments).
**Cost** price moves with `include` · cache 600 s
**Pricing** 5 credits for the video detail, stats and comments. `include=transcript` adds 10, which is exactly what the standalone transcript endpoint charges, so the bundle never costs more than running the two calls yourself.
**Streaming** Streams SSE when `include` includes `transcript`.
**Paging** none

**Query params**

- `url` (required) - Absolute http(s) URL of a YouTube, TikTok, Rumble, or Instagram video. · e.g. `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ`
- `comments` (optional, string) - How many top comments to fetch (0-50, default 20). `0` skips the comments leg.
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV of optional costed legs: `transcript` (adds the dedicated transcript leg, +10cr, refunded when null) and/or `commenter_profiles` (≤3 commenter mini-profiles, TikTok/Instagram in v1). · e.g. `transcript,commenter_profiles`
- `app_demand` (optional, boolean) - Optional. 1 reads the caption first, then the comments, and returns data.app_demand: late when the caption already names an app, otherwise the count of comments that want an app they do not have, the count that name one, and that ratio. The ratio is withheld unless the comments support it. A low-confidence comment is not counted. No extra credits.
- `claim` (optional, string) - Optional sentence. When set, data.sense_check says whether the comments support it, contradict it, or say nothing. A confidence under the cut, or one high-confidence contradiction, withholds the sentence. No extra credits.

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `comments.items`, `comments.next_cursor`, `comments.total`, `coverage`, `legs`, `partial_failure`, `video.computed.content_category`, `video.computed.engagement_rate` (+36 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/video-intel" \
  --data-urlencode "url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

## GET /v1/prism/voice - 5 credits (custom)

Fetches a handle's recent posts from four microblogs in parallel, time-merges them into one chronological feed, and computes platform presence, a cross-post rate, and a per-platform tone label (a soft LLM heuristic that degrades to absent on failure). Microblogs the handle isn't on return empty arrays with `platform_presence:false`: the absence map is the product. Flat 5cr; all-miss → full refund. The `legs[]` block reports each leg's status, cost, and latency. X pages: pass a prior `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. v1 is list-level (no per-post detail drill).

**Use when** you want to follow someone across microblogs in one call; creator-card returns their profile stats, this returns what they actually posted.
**Cost** cache 600 s
**Paging** cursor · page size not measured · depth unknown

**Query params**

- `handle` (required) - The handle to look up across all four microblogs (a single leading @ is stripped). · e.g. `nasa`
- `platforms` (optional, string) - CSV subset of twitter,threads,bluesky,truthsocial (default all four). · e.g. `twitter,threads,bluesky,truthsocial`
- `cursor` (optional, string) - Opaque composite cursor from a prior response's `next_cursor`. X/Twitter pages; Truth Social pages on `next_max_id`; a mangled token is a 400 at 0 credits.
- `include` (optional, string) - CSV subset of posts_by_platform,merged_timeline,computed to trim the payload (posts_by_platform is always returned).

**Response** `Analytics` object at `data` (inferred from a sample): `computed.cross_post_rate`, `computed.platform_presence.bluesky`, `computed.platform_presence.threads`, `computed.platform_presence.truthsocial`, `computed.platform_presence.twitter`, `computed.tone_by_platform.threads`, `computed.tone_by_platform.twitter`, `computed.tone_distribution.threads.combative` (+26 more).

```bash
curl -G "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/prism/voice" \
  --data-urlencode "handle=nasa" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```
